title: High-touch Request Orchard: aggregation and first-pass scoping for enterprise asks
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Sales and CS teams field high-touch enterprise asks that often arrive as multi-feature bundles (compliance, private deployment, observability, custom integrations). These get into a long queue with unclear priority and inconsistent scoping. Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable aggregation and first-pass scoping process (the 'Orchard') that clusters related asks, assigns an initial bucket and confidence-level estimate, surfaces key risks, and produces a 1-page readiness brief for PM/Eng review. This ticket defines the Orchard buckets, initial rubric, artifacts required from Sales/CS, and a pilot plan with two strategic enterprise accounts.

acceptance_criteria: Orchard baseline buckets defined and documented
Intake template (Sales/CS) live in Confluence and linked from Slack command
At least 10 existing open enterprise asks bucketed with initial estimates and risk notes
Pilot run with two accounts and metrics captured (TTR: time-to-first-scope <= 5 business days)
PM/Eng review gates produce clear next-step (scope, spike, or decline) for each ask
initial_scoping_notes: Bucket A: Private Deployment & Network (KV: VPC, on-prem install, egress rules) — typical effort: 5-13 pts, blockers: infra/network review, customer infra readiness.
Bucket B: Compliance & Data Residency (KV: KMS, audit logs, SOC2/ISO artifacts) — typical effort: 3-8 pts, blockers: legal templates, KMS integration complexity.
Bucket C: Performance / SLO Guarantees (KV: tail latency targets, p99, concurrency) — typical effort: 3-13 pts, blockers: benchmarking, Dedicated capacity sizing.
Bucket D: Console & Observability (KV: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards) — typical effort: 2-8 pts, blockers: metrics ingestion and retention policies.
Bucket E: Custom Integration & Workflow (KV: webhooks, custom auth, plugin connectors) — typical effort: 3-13 pts, blockers: API contract, security review.
Confidence bands: Low (spike required), Medium (rough implementation estimate), High (detailed PRD available). For pilot we mark confidence per ask.
risks: Over-bucketing: unrelated asks grouped together causing scope creep
Under-estimating infra work for private deployments (hidden operational costs)
Delays waiting on customer-provided artifacts (legal, network access)
Ambiguous success criteria from Sales leads to rework after scoping
